Authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have announced that the Ebola outbreak ravaging parts of the country has reached its peak.

For the first time since the epidemic was declared in May, the numbers of people becoming infected is slowing down, according to officials.

Brazil’s supreme court has been thrust into what experts consider the greatest crisis since the return of democracy in the 1980s, as two rival judges lock horns on the eve of the presidential election with unpredictable consequences for Latin America’s largest democracy.

A giant banner of Brazil’s incarcerated former president Jair Bolsonaro fluttered in the morning breeze as his eldest son, Flávio, touched down at an airfield on the fringe of a city that will soon help decide the future of one of the biggest democracies on earth.

Indonesian police are investigating the deaths of three Australians who died in Bali over the weekend, with initial reports suggesting a father killed his two young children before taking his own life.

Rescue workers in Indonesia said at least six people had died and 130 others were missing on Sunday after a ferry sailing between the islands of Java and Borneo capsized in bad weather.

The vessel, MV Matui, had set sail with more than 40 passengers and crew on Friday from the island of Santo to Ambae island in very rough seas, but did not arrive.

euronews.description: Mounting anger among police officers has been fuelled by a range of issues, including discontent around the special police duty allowance (ISSP), their "risk bonus", which has not gone up since 2019.

euronews.description: Carney made the comments at a two-day Investment Summit in Toronto as Canada seeks to diversify and bring new investment into the country.

euronews.description: Concerns are mounting that Europe's central macroeconomic institution might not be ready for turnover at the highest level.

euronews.description: Puigdemont, who fled to Belgium to avoid detention after the referendum and is still the target of an arrest warrant, has been accused of misusing public money to organise the 2017 independence referendum.

euronews.title: Two years after COP29, Azerbaijan turns climate commitments into investment
euronews.description: The country has committed €540 million to climate-resilient irrigation and launched an AI-based farmer-scoring system, developed with the FAO, to channel subsidies to smallholders who adopt water-saving and soil-regenerating techniques.

euronews.description: Turkish police detained at least 150 pro-LGBTQ protesters in Istanbul on Tuesday, 15 September, during a demonstration against a nationwide crackdown on the LGBTQ community.

euronews.title: Trump blasts Supreme Court over mail-in ballot ruling
euronews.description: Trump had sought to limit mail-in voting ahead of November's key midterm elections, which will determine the makeup of Congress for his final two years in office.

euronews.title: ‘Do you know where Ceuta is?’: EU Parliament erupts over migration
euronews.description: The European People’s Party and Socialists clashed in a heated European Parliament debate, with shouting and mutual accusations exposing deepening divisions over migration within the coalition backing Ursula von der Leyen.

euronews.title: US threatens EU with retaliation over European preference in EU budget
euronews.description: Washington said that the competitiveness fund included in the budget would “impede” partnership with the US because of provisions favouring “made in Europe” products.

euronews.title: How can Europe decarbonise without sacrificing economic development? New study offers roadmap
euronews.description: A new study suggests importing some of the materials used to make steel, fertilisers and chemicals could help Europe keep more manufacturing at home.

euronews.title: EU unveils digital platform to ease recognition of social security and professional qualifications
euronews.description: The European Commission estimates that a system allowing faster and easier recognition of working documents could save billions of euros by the end of the next decade.

euronews.title: Russia, Venezuela and Trump’s oil push: the EU's awkward G20 energy summit
euronews.description: EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen heads to the G20 energy meeting in Houston as Brussels’ clean-energy strategy clashes with Washington’s push for “energy abundance” through greater oil and gas production. The presence of Russian and Venezuelan officials adds a further geopolitical complication.

euronews.title: Von der Leyen will deliver an 'inspirational message' in annual speech, EU vice-president says
euronews.description: European Commission Vice-President Roxana Mînzatu hopes Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will deliver an "inspirational message" that will "speak directly to each of the 450 million Europeans" in her annual address to citizens.

rfi.title: Canada's Carney seeking closer EU ties, to attend State of the EU address
rfi.description: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney will become the first non-EU head of government to attend the State of the Union address as he seeks to bring Canada and the EU closer in the face of a hostile United States.

rfi.title: Workers across France stage protests over pay and rising costs
rfi.description: Protests are taking place across France on Tuesday, with fishermen, police officers, energy workers, university staff and other groups mobilising over a range of demands. Better pay, working conditions and the high cost of energy are among the main concerns.

rfi.title: Environmental activists angry over controversial AI data centre near Paris
rfi.description: France is preparing to build Europe’s largest artificial intelligence data centre in a village outside of Paris. The government hopes to boost its computing infrastructure and give France an edge in the global race to develop AI, but activists are concerned about the impacts on health and the environment.

rfi.title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Lithuania in latest Baltic security incident
rfi.description: NATO fighter jets shot have down a drone over Lithuania in the latest security incident on Europe's border with Russia as its war with Ukraine continues.

rfi.title: International justice 'can't be erased' despite US sanctions: ICC prosecutor
rfi.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) is facing US sanctions since deciding to issue arrest warrants over alleged war crimes in Gaza. Mame Mandiaye Niang, the Senegalese magistrate who has been acting head of the ICC's Office of the Prosecutor since his predecessor Karim Khan was forced out, tells RFI that while the Court's resilience is being tested, its existence is not under threat.

rfi.title: Finland joins French nuclear umbrella amid European security push
rfi.description: Finland has decided to join France’s nuclear deterrence umbrella in a bid to bolster regional security in the face of uncertainty over the United States' commitment to Europe and NATO.

rfi.title: France says Russia seeks to 'intimidate' EU with train attack near Poland
rfi.description: France and the European Union have condemned a Russian strike on a passenger train on the Polish border that has raised concerns about the risks of the war spreading closer to EU and NATO territory.

rfi.title: France seeks EU backing for revised social media ban for under-15s
rfi.description: A month after France’s Constitutional Council struck down a proposed social media ban for under-15s, the government has submitted a new version that President Emmanuel Macron wants passed before he leaves office in the spring.

rfi.title: World in Frames: RFI traces the stories behind the world's most famous photos
rfi.description: As France marks 200 years since inventor Nicéphore Niépce took the world’s oldest surviving photograph, RFI looks back at photos that changed our view of history – or even history itself. Here we tell the story of how a portrait of an unnamed woman came to represent the suffering of a nation in Dorothea Lange’s Migrant Mother, and what the iconic picture left out.

rfi.title: 'Historic day' for Nigeria as Dangote oil refinery launches IPO
rfi.description: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote on Monday launched what is slated as Africa's biggest initial public offering (IPO), which aims to raise $1.6 billion (€1.3 billion) to expand his mega oil refinery to become the world's largest.

rfi.title: Growing budgets show Africa keen to defend its place in the space race
rfi.description: African states invest around $500 million in space programmes annually, a figure expected to reach around $40 billion by 2030. With a number of initiatives already in place, the continent is seeking a seat at the table when it comes to international decisions on space exploration and equal access to the development of technology.

rfi.title: Normandy derailment inquiry widens focus on rail fragment found on track
rfi.description: A technical investigation has been launched into the derailment of a regional train near Rouen that left 44 people injured, as authorities work to establish how a piece of rail came to be lying on the track.

rfi.title: Sweden's election too close to call, left opposition narrowly leads
rfi.description: Sweden's general election is still too close to call, with Magdalena Andersson’s centre-left opposition coalition holding a narrow lead over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s right-wing alliance.

rfi.title: Macron, Carney to visit French Atlantic islands with sovereignty message to Trump
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney will visit the French North Atlantic territory of Saint-Pierre-and-Miquelon next week, in a symbolic show of support for national sovereignty amid renewed territorial claims by US President Donald Trump.

rfi.title: France moves to defuse US row over UN social media post
rfi.description: France has expressed regret over a social media post questioning the United States’ commitment to human rights, in a move expected to clear the way for its new ambassador to take up his post in Washington.

rfi.title: French Rafale jets take flight for 40,000-kilometre mission over three-continents
rfi.description: Four French Rafale fighter jets have embarked on a 40-day mission spanning three continents, highlighting France’s ability to deploy its air power around the world while strengthening cooperation with key international partners.

rfi.title: Radio France staff strike over appointment of right-wing magazine editor
rfi.description: Radio France staff began a two-day strike on Sunday over France Inter’s decision to hire a senior editor from the right-wing magazine Valeurs actuelles as a political commentator. Charles Sapin’s appointment has drawn criticism because the magazine has previously been convicted of racist public insult and incitement to racial hatred.

rfi.title: As catches dwindle, Congo River fishermen turn to plastic waste
rfi.description: On the Congo River, plastic is becoming the catch of the day. Some fishermen around Kinshasa, capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo, can now make more money pulling plastic from the water than catching fish, as declining catches and growing waste pollution threaten an artisanal way of life.

lemonde.title: Comment la Russie est devenue « l’Etat-FSB » : « On leur a donné le pays »
lemonde.description: « Le système Poutine » (2/3). Les élections législatives russes, prévues du 18 au 20 septembre, se dérouleront sans enjeu dans un pays muselé par le service fédéral de sécurité, dont les pouvoirs ne cessent de s’étendre, hors de tout contrôle, depuis l’invasion de l’Ukraine.

lemonde.title: Au procès de l’assassinat de Federico Martin Aramburu, la dernière heure du rugbyman racontée par son ami et témoin Shaun Hegarty
lemonde.description: Devant la cour d’assises de Paris, l’ancien rugbyman a fait le récit, mardi 15 septembre, de la soirée de 2022 qui a coûté la vie à l’international argentin, tué à la suite d’une banale altercation.

lemonde.title: Emmanuel Macron lance le nouveau service militaire national avec une première cohorte de 3 000 jeunes
lemonde.description: Le nouveau format, qui succède au service national universel, devra faire ses preuves. Notamment sur son financement et sur l’emploi des jeunes volontaires, qui pourront remplacer des militaires d’active sur des missions annexes.

lemonde.title: Loi intégrale sur les violences sexistes et sexuelles : Sébastien Lecornu s’engage mais reste flou sur les moyens supplémentaires
lemonde.description: Dans une tribune au « Monde », mardi 15 septembre, le premier ministre évoque pour la première fois une « trajectoire pluriannuelle » de moyens consacrés à la lutte contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles, mais reste muet sur les montants supplémentaires qui pourraient être engagés.

lemonde.title: Les faillites de restaurants se multiplient partout en France, entre charges en hausse et pouvoir d’achat des clients en baisse
lemonde.description: Plus de 4 900 établissements de la restauration sont en défaillance depuis le début de l’année, soit une hausse de 7 % comparée à la même période en 2025. Et l’été caniculaire n’a pas permis au secteur d’inverser la tendance.

lemonde.title: Les doms de Bénarès, impurs gardiens des bûchers mortuaires indiens
lemonde.description: Dans les ghats, ces escaliers qui plongent dans les eaux sacrées du Gange, seuls les doms peuvent assurer la gestion des bûchers funéraires. Issus de la caste des intouchables, ils sont pourtant considérés comme les intermédiaires choisis entre le bas monde et l’au-delà.

lemonde.title: L’intrigante et soudaine mansuétude de la France à l’égard de l’oligarque russe Alicher Ousmanov
lemonde.description: A la surprise de ses partenaires européens, Paris demande que le milliardaire, réputé proche de Vladimir Poutine, soit retiré de la liste des sanctions contre des personnalités russes.

lemonde.title: Catherine Ringer, célèbre voix des Rita Mitsouko, est morte à l’âge de 68 ans
lemonde.description: La chanteuse s’était fait connaître grâce au succès du groupe Les Rita Mitsouko, formé avec Fred Chichin, et notamment de leurs tubes « Marcia Baïla » et « Andy ».

lemonde.title: Rachida Dati devant le tribunal correctionnel de Paris dans l’affaire Ghosn-Renault
lemonde.description: A partir de mercredi, l’ancienne ministre est jugée notamment pour « corruption passive » et « trafic d’influence passif » pour 900 000 euros perçus, entre 2009 et 2013, de l’ex-PDG de Renault-Nissan Carlos Ghosn, lui aussi renvoyé.

lemonde.title: Patricio Guzman, cinéaste et documentariste du Chili d’Allende à Pinochet, est mort
lemonde.description: Multirécompensé, le réalisateur était connu pour avoir réalisé, entre 1972 et 1973, « La Bataille du Chili », trilogie de cinq heures sur le gouvernement de l’ancien président socialiste chilien Salvador Allende. Il est mort à l’âge de 85 ans.

lemonde.title: Formation professionnelle : l’AFPA va licencier plus de 800 personnes
lemonde.description: L’Agence nationale pour la formation professionnelle des adultes, organisme public qui emploie 5 410 salariés, souffre notamment de la concurrence du privé. Son plan vise à combler un déficit chronique de l’activité d’ici trois ans

lemonde.title: Violences dans le périscolaire parisien : Anne Hidalgo renvoie à un « échec collectif »
lemonde.description: Auditionnée devant les sénateurs de la commission d’enquête sur la prévention et le traitement des violences dans ce secteur, l’ancienne maire de Paris a regretté des « dysfonctionnements » dont elle a refusé d’endosser seule la responsabilité.

lemonde.title: La direction de Radio France maintient Charles Sapin sur France Inter, les syndicats déposent un nouveau préavis de grève
lemonde.description: Des syndicats de France Télévisions s’élèvent aussi contre le directeur adjoint de la rédaction de « Valeurs actuelles », qui, le 13 septembre sur la chaîne Franceinfo, a défendu « la priorité nationale » dans l’attribution des logements sociaux.

lemonde.title: A l’université, la rentrée des étudiants étrangers perturbée par la généralisation des droits d’inscription différenciés
lemonde.description: Un décret paru en mai impose aux universités un maximum de 30 % d’étudiants extra-européens pouvant être exonérés de frais d’inscription. Les établissements mettent en place des procédures variables pour évaluer les recours. Les présidents d’université craignent que cette mesure fasse baisser le nombre d’inscrits.

lemonde.title: En Turquie, la vague d’arrestations dans la communauté LGBT+ se poursuit
lemonde.description: Recep Tayyip Erdogan, qui a proclamé en 2026 « la décennie de la famille », prend régulièrement pour cible les personnes LGBT+, qu’il qualifie de « perverses » et auxquelles il impute la chute drastique de la natalité.

lemonde.title: Sénatoriales 2026 : une augmentation notable du nombre de députés candidats
lemonde.description: Trente-trois députés figurent parmi les quelque 1 600 candidats aux élections qui se tiendront le 27 septembre. Un nombre en forte hausse, dans la lignée d’une tendance déjà observée aux élections municipales de mars.

france24fr.title: Sans son nom dessus, Donald Trump menace de ne pas rouvrir le Kennedy Center
france24fr.description: Le conseil d'administration du Kennedy Center à Washington, largement acquis à Donald Trump, a voté sa fermeture immédiate mardi, quelques heures après qu'un juge fédéral a interdit d'inscrire sur ce haut lieu culturel une référence au président sans l'accord du Congrès.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : les inquiétantes routes des combattants africains recrutés par la Russie
france24fr.description: Nous consacrons cette édition à un phénomène inquiétant : l'enrôlement de jeunes africains dans les rang de l'armée russe pour combattre sur le front ukrainien. Souvent, ils ne savent pas qu'ils partent pour la guerre et pensent voyager pour un obtenir un nouveau travail. Beaucoup de combattants sont morts sur le champ de bataille. Nous en parlons avec Noé Michalon, journaliste auteur d'une enquête pour Africa Intelligence, et Karfa Diallo, président de l'association Mémoires et partages.

france24fr.title: Équipe de France : le staff de Zidane au complet avant son premier rassemblement à Clairefontaine
france24fr.description: Entouré de fidèles comme David Bettoni ou Hamidou Msaidie, issus de son aventure au Real Madrid, le nouveau sélectionneur des Bleus Zinedine Zidane a constitué une équipe complète, du préparateur physique au chef cuisinier en passant par Fabien Barthez aux gardiens. Un rassemblement inédit de deux semaines et demie est prévu à Clairefontaine avant le match du 25 septembre en Turquie.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : heurts et gaz lacrymogène lors de rassemblements de l'opposition
france24fr.description: En RD Congo, la coalition d’opposition C64 a manifesté dans les rues de Kinshasa. Depuis plusieurs mois ses membres s’opposent au projet de changement de la Constitution porté par la majorité au pouvoir. Une manifestation alors que s’ouvre la rentrée parlementaire pour les députés congolais. Reportage d'Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula.

france24fr.title: En France, la colère monte face aux prix du carburant en hausse
france24fr.description: Le carburant coûte de plus en plus cher en France : 2,68€ le litre de diesel et 2,49€ pour l'essence. La guerre au Moyen-Orient et les blocages du détroit d'Ormuz, où transitait 20% du gaz et du pétrole mondiaux, et du détroit de Bab El-Madeb, qui explique ces augmentations. Parallèlement, la demande française pour le diesel n'a pas baissé, ce carburant étant utilisé par la moitié des véhicules particuliers et dans l'industrie, de la pêche au transport routier en passant par l'agriculture.

france24fr.title: Drone abattu en Lituanie, fusées tirées au Danemark : l'UE dénonce des "provocations" russes
france24fr.description: La cheffe de l'UE Ursula von der Leyen a dénoncé mardi le comportement "irresponsable et dangereux" de la Russie après que le Danemark s'est plaint de tirs de fusées éclairantes contre un de ses hélicoptères, et que des avions de l'Otan ont dû abattre un drone en Lituanie.

france24fr.title: Sommet des Brics : un selfie de Poutine généré par IA partagé par les ambassades d’Iran et de Russie
france24fr.description: De prétendus selfies de Vladimir Poutine avec des chefs d'États lors du récent sommet des Brics ont été partagés par des ambassades d'Iran et de Russie ainsi que par une porte-parole du BJP. Ces images ont été générées par intelligence artificielle

france24fr.title: Radiographe du Chili et de ses blessures, le réalisateur Patricio Guzman s'est éteint
france24fr.description: Le cinéaste et documentariste chilien Patricio Guzman, qui a notamment filmé la chute de Salvador Allende et le coup d'Etat du général Pinochet en 1973, est décédé mardi à Paris à l'âge de 85 ans. Il vivait en France depuis les années 80 d'où il menait avec ses films un infatigable travail contre l'amnésie.

france24fr.title: De faux clichés de Poutine au sommet des BRICS diffusés par les ambassades d’Iran et de Russie
france24fr.description: Le 18e sommet des BRICS se tenait les 12 et le 13 septembre à New Delhi, en Inde. Et pour célébrer la tenue du sommet, deux selfies de Vladimir Poutine accompagné de ses homologues ont été publiés par des comptes officiels : les ambassades de Russie et d'Iran. Problème : ils sont faux, et sont utilisés à des fins politiques. Décryptage avec Jules BOITEAU.

france24fr.title: IA : l'humanité en danger ? Les dirigeants du secteur tirent la sonnette d’alarme
france24fr.description:
L’IA peut-elle, va-t-elle, détruire l’humanité ?
 
La question n’est plus réservée à la science-fiction. Après la démission du chercheur d’Anthropic Jacob Coxon, qui affirme que ceux qui développent l’IA pensent sincèrement qu’elle pourrait « tous nous tuer avant la fin de la décennie », plusieurs chercheurs d’Anthropic, d’OpenAI et de DeepMind disent partager cette crainte. Le patron d’Anthropic, Dario Amodei, appelle lui aussi l’industrie à ralentir.

france24fr.title: Face aux dangers de l'IA, des acteurs majeurs travaillent à la création d'un organe de supervision
france24fr.description: Alors que se multiplient les appels à mieux contrôler les dérives de l’intelligence artificielle (IA), OpenAI a déclaré mardi à l’AFP qu’elle travaille avec Anthropic et Google DeepMind à la création d’un organe de supervision des risques liés à l’IA.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : les victimes de l'incendie meurtrier de Bukavu inhumées
france24fr.description: 🇨🇩 En RDC, un dernier hommage a été rendu aux victimes de l’incendie d’une école le 10 septembre à Bukavu. La cérémonie a eu lieu en présence des familles et des responsables du M23 qui contrôle la zone. Au moins 26 enfants ont péri dans le drame, selon l’UNICEF.

france24fr.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : la flamme olympique a entamé sa tournée au Sénégal
france24fr.description: 🇸🇳 Au Sénégal, la flamme olympique a entamé sa tournée, à 45 jours des JO de la jeunesse. Première étape, Dakar la capitale, avant un parcours dans les 14 régions du pays.

france24fr.title: Budget 2027 : Lecornu propose 1,5 milliard d'euros contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu a annoncé mardi les budgets qu’il entend allouer à la "loi intégrale" contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles, qui sera discutée au Parlement à l’automne 2026. Le gouvernement proposera de consacrer environ 1,5 milliard d'euros à la lutte contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles et 2,6 milliards pour la protection de l'enfance.

france24fr.title: Syrie : 10 morts dans une émeute à Kobané
france24fr.description: À Kobané, dans le nord de la Syrie, une manifestation après le meurtre d’un ancien combattant kurde a dégénéré en violences et en arrestations. Des dizaines de personnes ont été interpellées et conduites à la prison de la ville, encore administrée par les anciennes autorités kurdes malgré l’intégration des forces de sécurité à l’État syrien. Cet épisode illustre les difficultés de la transition engagée depuis l’accord conclu en janvier entre Damas et les Forces démocratiques syriennes (FDS). Les

france24fr.title: Sécheresse record en France: les conséquences sur l'Agriculture
france24fr.description: La France traverse une sécheresse record. 61% des nappes phréatiques de l'Hexagone ont un taux de remplissage en dessous des normales pour un mois de septembre. Et cette sécheresse a des conséquences pour l'agriculture. Si la production de blé a pu être maintenue, le maïs et les légumes ont vu leurs rendements très affectés. Plusieurs enseignes de grandes distribution ont, en conséquence, décidé d'accepter les légumes et fruits "moches" pour assurer l'approvisionnement des consommateurs.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle au Brésil : Leonardo Di Caprio s'engage aux côtés de Lula da Silva, président sortant
france24fr.description: Un acteur américain s'est invité dans la campagne présidentielle brésilienne. Début septembre, Leonardo Di Caprio s'est affiché avec Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, le président sortant. Un cliché fait pour porter plusieurs messages, notamment sur la préservation de l'environnement et la défense des peuples indigènes. Les précisions de Marine Resse, correspondante France 24 à Rio de Janeiro.

france24fr.title: Aux Emmy Awards, "Widow's Bay" et Matthew Rhys battent des records
france24fr.description: Au programme de cette émission 100% séries de A l'Affiche ! : La 78ème cérémonie des Emmy Awards avec la série " Widow's Bay" qui a littéralement englouti la concurrence. La comédie horrifique d’Apple TV repart avec quatorze statuettes, un record pour une comédie sur une seule saison.

zeit.title: Ed Sheeran: Vorgruppen verlassen Tour von Ed Sheeran nach Rauswurf von Macklemore
zeit.description: Wegen propalästinensischer Äußerungen wurde Macklemore als Vorband von Ed Sheeran gestrichen. Nun haben sich alle Acts aus Solidarität aus der Tournee zurückgezogen.

zeit.description: Boris Pistorius und sein Amtskollege Pete Hegseth wollen bei der Produktion von Waffen stärker kooperieren. Die USA haben deutschen Investitionen in Verteidigung gelobt.

zeit.description: Ein Gericht hatte Donald Trump wiederholt die Anbringung seines Namens an der Fassade des Kennedy Centers untersagt. Nun lässt er das nationale Kulturzentrum schließen.

zeit.title: TV-Runde vor MV-Wahl: Peters rechnet fest mit CDU-Einzug in den Schweriner Landtag
Künstliche Intelligenz: KI‑Konzerne OpenAI, Anthropic und Google wollen sich selbst regulieren
zeit.description: OpenAI, Anthropic und Google planen eine gemeinsame Aufsichtsorganisation für KI. US-Präsident Donald Trump hatte zuvor eine staatliche Regulierung abgelehnt.

zeit.title: Ali al-Saidi in Berlin: Irak bietet Deutschland Vereinbarungen über Öllieferungen an
zeit.description: Iraks Ministerpräsident Al-Saidi hat in Berlin Öllieferungen in Aussicht gestellt. Der Kanzler drang auf ein »gutes Miteinander« der Regierung mit den Kurden im Norden.

zeit.title: Ukraine: Wladimir Putins extreme Botschaft
zeit.description: Russland greift einen Zug mit westlichen Politikern an. Dahinter steckt eine Strategie, die schon im Kalten Krieg angewendet wurde – und die Deutschland anstachelt.

nzz.title: Eishockey National League: ZSC siegt trotz dreimaligem Rückstand
nzz.description: Die ZSC Lions ringen den SCB beim National-League-Saisonstart mit 5:3 nieder. Es ist die beste aktuelle Serie eines Teams beim Saisonstart. Meister Fribourg ging in Biel derweil mit 2:4 unter.

nzz.title: Sion springt in der Super League auf Tabellenrang 2
nzz.description: Der FC Sion erringt den vierten Sieg in Folge. Ein Doppelwechsel nach einer Stunde sorgt bei den Grasshoppers für den Unterschied und das Endresultat 5:2.

nzz.title: «Ewigkeitschemikalien»: Der Ständerat verschafft den Bauern Zeit, um sich auf strengere PFAS-Regeln einzustellen
nzz.description: Wieder prägt der Kanton St. Gallen die PFAS-Debatte: Ein Mitte-Ständerat setzt sich für einen pragmatischeren Umgang ein.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Das neue «Stadtfest» ist entlarvend: Zürich dachte einst gross. Jetzt denkt es klein
nzz.description: Der rot-grüne Stadtrat will kein Züri-Fäscht mehr – es soll «dezentral» und im Kleinen gefeiert werden. Es ist ein Rückzug ins Kleingeistige.

nzz.title: Das Züri-Fäscht kehrt 2029 zurück – neu aber als «dezentrale» Feier fern des Seebeckens. Ohne Feuerwerk und Flugshow
nzz.description: Das neue Fest soll entlang der Ufer von Sihl und Limmat stattfinden. Ein Element von früher bleibe aber erhalten, versprechen die Organisatoren.

nzz.title: Leihmutterschaft ist in der Schweiz verboten, doch die Fälle nehmen zu. Die Justizdirektorin Jacqueline Fehr warnt: «Da kommt ein grosses Problem auf uns zu»
nzz.description: Seit Jahrzehnten drücke sich das nationale Parlament vor seiner Verantwortung, sagt die Zürcher SP-Magistratin. Und fordert eine Lösung.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Migrationskrise in Europa: Polens Grenzschutz stoppt Kühltransporter mit Migranten
nzz.description: Über die griechischen Inseln, die Balkanroute oder den Ärmelkanal versuchen noch immer täglich Migranten, unter Lebensgefahr nach Europa zu gelangen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Bundesrat Martin Pfister muss das VBS durchleuchten – bis in den letzten Winkel
nzz.description: Er sorge sich um «die Vertrauensarbeit im VBS», sagte Martin Pfister am Dienstag im Nationalrat. Als Departementschef darf er das. Als Bundesrat müsste ihm das verlorengegangene Vertrauen in das VBS mehr Kummer bereiten.

nzz.title: Einheitliche Berufe in Europa: Die EU will dies endlich ermöglichen, Verbände melden Protest an
nzz.description: Für EU-Bürger und Schweizer soll es einfacher werden, in Europa einen Job anzunehmen. Die EU will daher Berufe vereinheitlichen und so den Binnenmarkt vertiefen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - KI-Firmen können sich die Angstmacherei mit dem Ende der Menschheit sparen
nzz.description: Firmen wie Open AI und Anthropic behaupten, sie würden die KI-Entwicklung nun verlangsamen. Es wäre naiv zu glauben, sie täten dies aus ethischen Gründen. Statt ihre Besorgnis um das Wohl der Menschheit zu inszenieren, sollten sie jene Schäden mindern, die ihre Tools bereits heute verursachen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: Ruag baut bis zu 49 Stellen ab +++ Ständerat Hannes Germann tritt nicht mehr zur Wahl an
Dokumentarfilm «Naza»: In Venedig gefeiert, in Jerusalem als Verrat gebrandmarkt
nzz.description: Zwei Filmemacher werfen Israels Armee schwere Verfehlungen in Gaza vor. Nun fordert ein Minister ihre Ausbürgerung.

nzz.title: Der Ölschock trifft die Schweiz weniger als andere Länder. Doch wieso wird Diesel deutlich teurer als Benzin?
nzz.description: Die steigenden Energiepreise belasten die Schweizer Konsumenten im internationalen Vergleich wenig. Am stärksten leidet, wer auf Diesel angewiesen ist. Dort ist die Knappheit grösser als beim Benzin.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Verwaltungsrat von Migros Online stellt sich neu auf
DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Gerät die KI «ausser Kontrolle»? Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten zur Debatte um die Sicherheit der künstlichen Intelligenz

nzz.title: VIDEO - Die Ernährungsinitiative im Überblick
nzz.description: Die Initiative von Umweltaktivistin Franziska Herren fordert eine radikale Umgestaltung der Schweizer Landwirtschaft. Was bedeutet das konkret für Teller und Markt?

observador.title: Clooney "herói", Passos censurado e Montenegro elogiado
observador.description: Num dia em que o MP fez poucas perguntas, o ex-PM 'embrulhou-se' nas escutas sobre a casa de Paris e citou ator George Clooney para dizer que se sentia melancólico sobre Portugal.

observador.title: Ucrânia testa com sucesso novo intercetor de drones a jato
observador.description: Zelensky anunciou que a Ucrânia testou com sucesso um novo sistema de interceção para combater os drones de ataque russos a jato. O feito é o principal destaque de hoje do The Kyiv Independent.

observador.title: Mourinho brincou com o fogo mas com Espí nunca se queima
observador.description: Após uma primeira parte com dois golos, um anulado e várias oportunidades, Real desceu, deixou que Elche acreditasse e só voltou a acordar quando Carlos Espí saiu do banco para desfazer empate (2-3).

observador.title: As notícias das 22h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Mulher morre atropelada à porta de casa em Barcelos
observador.description: Além da vítima mortal, os ocupantes do carro ficaram feridos. O alerta foi dado às 18h57, tendo o óbito da vítima sido declarado no local.

observador.title: Elisa Ferreira defende "regionalização sem dramas"
observador.description: A antiga governante lembra que é a favor da regionalização "há muitos anos". Desvaloriza o "drama nacional" no país acerca do assunto, dizendo que apenas é uma questão de organização administrativa.

observador.title: Lisboa sem data para fecho de metro de Santa Apolónia
observador.description: Em causa estão obras do Plano Geral de Drenagem de Lisboa, previstas para o início do ano e entretanto adiadas. Moedas realça "obra histórica", ainda em articulação com o Metropolitano.

observador.title: Cineastas mostram apoio a autores de documentário sobre Gaza
observador.description: Várias organizações apelaram às autoridades israelitas para que cessem as ameaças a realizadores de documentário sobre massacre. Cineastas israelitas assinam petição a favor da liberdade de expressão.

observador.title: Rússia e Ucrânia preparam medida para a reunificar famílias
observador.description: De acordo com a agência de notícias estatal TASS, a Comissária para os Direitos Humanos da Rússia confirmou um novo programa humanitário que se destina a reunificar famílias e crianças

observador.title: Crime e boxe. O homem que pagou casamento de filho de Trump
observador.description: Começou no boxe, foi condenado por dois crimes e um clube de motards mudou-lhe a vida, conhecendo rostos do Kremlin. Umar Kremlev lidera Associação Internacional de Boxe e é próximo do filho de Trump.

observador.title: Cavaco Silva critica "ruído político e mediático"
observador.description: Na entrega do Prémio Champalimaud, em Lisboa, ex-Presidente deixou aparente defesa do Governo. Já António José Seguro reforçou apelo ao pacto para a saúde.

observador.title: As notícias das 21h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Resolvida situação de 295 alunos sem colocação em escolas
observador.description: Diretor de agrupamento em Sintra disse, após reunião com o Ministério da Educação, que os alunos que ainda não tinham confirmação foram já distribuídos. Por colocar ficam apenas situações individuais.

observador.title: Prémio Champalimaud distingue investigação que devolve visão
observador.description: Apesar dos avanços, "continuam a ser escassos os tratamentos capazes de restabelecer uma visão funcional após a perda", situação que investigadores premiados "ajudaram a mudar", indica fundação.

observador.title: Cavaco: "Ruído mediático é muito pouco justificativo"
observador.description: Antigo Chefe de Estado considera que o "ruído" não é benéfico para os interesses do país. António José Seguro voltou a apelar à necessidade de um pacto para a saúde.

observador.title: Marco Silva fala em Benfica "longe" do que pretende
observador.description: "Águias" enfrentam esta quarta-feira o clube de Milão. Técnico dos encarnados antevê dificuldades no jogo em San Siro. "Ainda estamos longe [do que queremos]".

observador.title: Governo quer taxa de 33% nas petrolíferas para apoios
observador.description: A contribuição, de caráter temporário, incide sobre a parcela do lucro tributável de 2026 que exceda "em mais de 20%" a média dos lucros tributáveis registados em 2024 e 2025.

observador.title: Venezuela. Alex Saab declara-se culpado de corrupção nos EUA
observador.description: Alex Saab admitiu ter cometido diversos crimes financeiros. Após acordo com o Ministério Público norte-americano, alterou a sua declaração prévia de inocência, podendo enfrentar 20 anos de prisão.

spiegel.title: Lionel Messi spielt noch einmal für Argentinien
spiegel.description: Für einen Abschied in Argentinien: Der eigentlich längst zurückgetretene Lionel Messi kehrt für ein Spiel in die Nationalmannschaft zurück. Gegner in dem Freundschaftsspiel wird Benin.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz: Zum Durchschnaufen muss der Kanzler in der Keller
spiegel.description: Aufmunterung in schweren Zeiten: Bei der Adenauer-Stiftung wird Friedrich Merz freundlich empfangen und demonstriert Entschlossenheit. Doch seine Pläne für die kommenden Tage zeigen, wie heikel die Lage für den Kanzler ist.

spiegel.title: Kennedy Center: Von Donald Trump eingesetzte Führung beschließt Schließung
spiegel.description: Das renommierte Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C. soll mit Verweis auf angeblich dringend notwendige Renovierungsarbeiten sofort schließen. Trump wollte zuvor unbedingt seinen Namen an der Stätte verewigt sehen.

spiegel.title: Ralf Richter ist tot: Ein Typ für die Ewigkeit
spiegel.description: Vokuhila, Schnauzer, Kult-Gangster: Niemand hatte den Ruhrpott-Malocher so drauf wie Ralf Richter. Mit seinen Rollen war er manchmal näher an der Realität, als für ihn gut gewesen wäre. Nun ist der Schauspieler gestorben.

spiegel.title: Ed Sheeran: Veranstalter entschied laut über Macklemore-Aus bei Tour
spiegel.description: Nach propalästinensischen Aussagen im Vorprogramm muss US-Rapper Macklemore die Tour von Ed Sheeran verlassen. Der meldet sich nun zu Wort – und erklärt, warum er sich öffentlich nicht politisch äußert.

spiegel.title: Jens Spahn gibt Bezirksvorsitz im Münsterland auf – NRW-Schulministerin Feller folgt
spiegel.description: Jens Spahn hat nach dem Verzicht auf den Posten als Bezirksvorsitzender der CDU im Münsterland kein Parteiamt mehr inne – das erste Mal seit Jahrzehnten. Seine Nachfolgerin wird NRW-Schulministerin Dorothee Feller.

spiegel.title: Russlands Angriffe an Polens Grenze: »Wir sollten die Kosten auf russischer Seite erhöhen«
spiegel.description: Russland rückt bei seinen Angriffen gegen die Ukraine immer näher an Nato-Gebiet heran. Der Sicherheitsexperte Aleksander Olech fordert die Bündnisstaaten auf, russische Drohnen künftig frühzeitig abzuschießen.

spiegel.title: Nahost: Die Huthis kontrollieren eine Meerenge - und sind mit Iran verbündet
spiegel.description: Sie sind denkbar schlecht ausgerüstet und trotzdem haben die mit Iran verbündeten Huthis die Kontrolle über eine wichtige Meerenge am Roten Meer übernommen. Geschafft haben sie das mit Kampfmoral, Erfindergeist und wohl auch mit KI.

spiegel.title: Fall Fabian: Der Richter konfrontiert Gina H. mit Widersprüchen ihrer Aussagen
spiegel.description: Der Richter konfrontiert Gina H. im Prozess um den getöteten Fabian stundenlang mit den Widersprüchen in ihren Aussagen. Die Mutter des toten Jungen hat nur eine Frage. Und die Angeklagte reagiert genervt.

spiegel.title: Hamburger SV: Vier Jahre saß er eine Dopingsperre ab, jetzt klammert sich der HSV an Mario Vušković
spiegel.description: Der Kroate Mario Vušković wurde 2022 positiv auf Epo getestet. In Hamburg galt er trotzdem als Opfer eines kaputten Systems. Nun kehrt er zum Club zurück. Kann er seine Karriere noch retten? Und mithin den taumelnden HSV?

spiegel.title: Elektroauto gebraucht kaufen: Spritpreis-Schock verknappt das Angebot günstiger Stromer
spiegel.description: Sprit ist teuer wie nie – viele Autofahrer wollen rasch auf einen Elektro-Pkw umsteigen. Doch auf Neuwagen müssen sie lange warten, die Preise für Gebrauchte heben ab. Welche Modelle noch relativ gut zu haben sind.

spiegel.title: Niedersachsen: AfD kann mehr als 250 Sitze in Kreis- und Gemeinderäten nicht besetzen
spiegel.description: Die AfD hat bei den Kommunalwahlen in Niedersachsen deutlich hinzugewonnen. Dennoch bleiben viele Sitze in Gemeinderäten leer, weil die Partei zu wenig Kandidierende aufgestellt hat. Was das für die Politik vor Ort bedeutet.

spiegel.title: Wahlkampf in Berlin: »Das war der dümmste Nazi, aber mit dem allerbesten Timing«
spiegel.description: Der jüdische Grünenpolitiker Daniel Eliasson wurde im Wahlkampf von einem Mann angegriffen und antisemitisch beleidigt. Was macht das mit einem, der täglich Hunderte Menschen ansprechen muss?

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz sagt Reise zur Uno-Generaldebatte nach New York ab

undark.title: Review: A Vision of a Future Where Machines Fight Wars
undark.description: In “Lethal Autonomy,” Frank Kendall, a former top defense department official, envisions a military future where vehicles and weapons operate largely on their own — including making some decisions to strike people or infrastructure. And in his view, conflict is coming to space, making it all more urgent.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

Researchers at the U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) Agricultural Research Service (ARS) are employing predictive models as part of a forward-thinking approach to manage New World screwworm. phys-org.description: No, President Joe Biden did not engineer Hurricane Milton. No, the ice crystal contrails left behind by high-altitude aircraft are not "chemtrails" sprayed by governments to control the weather or manipulate populations. No, state-run cloud seeding did not cause the record floods in Dubai.

phys-org.title: What are best options for controlling GSL dust, and what would they cost?
phys-org.description: A new collaborative report from University of Utah researchers and coordinated by the Wilkes Center for Climate Science & Policy provides Utah Department of Natural Resources, Department of Environmental Quality and policymakers with a comprehensive analysis of the growing risks posed by dust from the exposed lakebed of Great Salt Lake, the potential costs of controlling that dust, and the long-term benefits of stabilizing lake levels.

phys-org.title: Webb reveals dynamic panorama of star formation, including smallest known brown dwarfs
phys-org.description: This starry view of the nearby star-forming region IC 348 is one of the largest images released to date from NASA's James Webb Space Telescope. Using Webb, astronomers searched IC 348 for brown dwarfs, which are less massive than the smallest stars. The researchers discovered brown dwarfs just twice the mass of Jupiter, bringing the study of these curious objects into a new mass range and revealing new insights about the star-formation process.

phys-org.title: Disordered atoms steer shared light pulses by matching motion and timing
phys-org.description: A research team at the Institute of Applied Physics at TU Darmstadt has shown for the first time that atoms that are completely disordered and in constant motion can nevertheless emit jointly directed light preferentially in one direction—even though neither the atoms nor their environment exhibit a direction—and that the strength of this asymmetry can be specifically adjusted. The paper is published in the journal Physical Review Letters.

phys-org.title: Skipping showers is the latest trend. But is there any science to 'pheromone' maxxing?
phys-org.description: Across parts of the internet where young men trade tips on self-improvement, the latest project is scent. Deodorant is out, and washing less is in.

phys-org.title: Why most rivers don't respond to storms the same way twice
phys-org.description: The same amount of rain falling on the same landscape at different times can send very different amounts of water into its rivers, according to a new study in Nature Water. The research offers a global picture of how catchments behave—not where rivers are or how much water they carry, but how consistently landscapes turn rainfall into river flow.

phys-org.title: How a pathogen turns flowers into leaves
phys-org.description: Scientists have found how a protein produced by bacteria disrupts the mechanism that controls flower development in plants, turning reproductive organs into leaf-like structures. These findings shed light on a plant disease that is expected to spread as climate change expands the range of its insect vectors in northern latitudes. They used a synchrotron technique at ESRF, the European Synchrotron in Grenoble, France. The results are an Editor's Pick in the Journal of Biological Chemistry.

phys-org.title: Smart nanoparticles deliver antibiotics directly to H. pylori
phys-org.description: Helicobacter pylori bacteria infect around half the global population and are a leading cause of stomach ulcers and gastric cancer. While antibiotics remain the standard treatment, they often fail to reach bacteria hidden beneath the stomach's protective mucus layer and deep within ulcer tissue. This often requires higher antibiotic doses, increasing the risk of adverse effects and antibiotic resistance.

phys-org.title: Adaptive crystal can selectively capture CO₂ and recognize similar molecules
phys-org.description: Chemical separation can be energy-intensive when molecules have similar sizes and properties. Researchers from Shibaura Institute of Technology, Japan, have now developed an interlayer adaptive crystal that changes its spacing to recognize specific molecules.

phys-org.title: Magnets could help quantum computers talk to each other, says researcher
phys-org.description: Xufeng Zhang is using magnets to make computers more power efficient at the quantum level. The Northeastern professor of electrical and computer engineering recently published two papers highlighting small-scale magnetic systems he and his team developed that could help make computers much more power efficient in the future.

phys-org.title: Home advantage or pastures new? High-Arctic shorebirds rarely return to the same breeding area
phys-org.description: Shorebirds are capable of some of the longest migrations on Earth, yet most return year after year to the same area to breed. Coming back has distinct advantages, including knowing the best spots to feed or roost, having information about where predators lurk, and—hopefully—finding last year's partner again.

phys-org.title: Great Salt Lake's ancient past reveals how quickly fresh water can disappear
phys-org.description: From a mountainside overlooking Utah's Great Salt Lake, a time traveler turning back the clock 20,000 years would watch a dramatic transformation of the landscape. The shallow, salty lake below would swell into an immense body of fresh water, at one point reaching nearly 1,000 feet (305 meters) deep and covering more than 10 times the lake's modern area. Mountain ranges would become islands, and the new shoreline would move far beyond its current boundary.

phys-org.title: New peanut genome map uncovers hidden gene, boosts dense-planting yields 20%
phys-org.description: An international team that includes researchers from Murdoch University's Centre for Crop and Food Innovation (CCFI) has built the most comprehensive genetic map of the peanut yet and used this new genomic resource to breed a higher-yielding dwarf peanut line.

phys-org.title: Not all roads lead to Rome: Research challenges what we think we know about Roman roads
phys-org.description: A multidisciplinary team of researchers from Aarhus University in Denmark, Queen Mary University of London and other European institutions analyzed a data set representing almost 300,000 kilometers (186,000 miles) of Roman roads across the former empire, creating the most detailed quantitative picture yet of how the Roman road network was structured.

phys-org.title: Drought-flood alternation under climate change
phys-org.description: Climate change is increasing the frequency of both droughts and floods, meaning back-to-back extreme events are also on the rise. These rapidly alternating crises can harm people in complex ways. For example, back-to-back climate extremes can stress crops, reducing yields.

phys-org.title: Mitotic chromosomes may assemble from pre-existing chromatin 'building blocks' during cell division
phys-org.description: Inside each human cell, about 2 meters (6.6 feet) of genomic DNA must be accurately copied and equally transmitted to two daughter cells during cell division. To achieve this, the copied DNA is condensed into thick, short structures called mitotic chromosomes. However, how chromatin is organized and condensed to form mitotic chromosomes has long remained a major question in genetics and cell biology.

phys-org.title: Is science journalism dying? Comparing a 'science crash' 40 years ago to today
phys-org.description: When two popular science magazines—out of about 17 in circulation—ceased publication in the same year, one commentator said, "The science magazines didn't shake out. They fell apart." The general manager of one of the failed magazines said, "There was a perception that they were irrelevant." One of the publishers remembered being in a "state of shock" as the failures emerged.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Asset Europe Has Overlooked
proj-syn.description: Europe’s soil is gradually dying, and yet the continent has still not recognized it as a strategic asset. Fortunately, the EU has many of the tools it needs to act, but doing so will require an overarching framework that helps farmers access financial rewards for measurable soil outcomes.

proj-syn.title: Why India Wants Peace in Ukraine—and China Doesn’t
proj-syn.description: The Ukraine war has turned Russia into a junior partner of China. This serves China's economic and strategic interests, but it creates major risks for India, which has long counted on Russia to help it counterbalance Chinese influence in the region.

proj-syn.title: AI and the Broken Career Ladder
proj-syn.description: AI can broaden access to expertise, support innovation, and boost economic growth. But shared prosperity will depend less on the performance of the next frontier model than on our ability to preserve skill formation, reorganize work, and distribute the gains equitably.

proj-syn.title: AI Firms’ Self-Serving Warnings
proj-syn.description: There is a method to the frontier AI labs’ marketing madness. They claim that AI will not only replace workers and expand the potential market from software budgets to labor-saving applications, but also that the existential risk associated with the technology justifies curtailing additional capital spending.

proj-syn.title: The UN Cannot—and Need Not—Wait for Consensus
proj-syn.description: Although the United Nations system remains the foundation of global governance, its capacity to drive domestic implementation of urgently needed reforms and regulations is stretched thin. Fortunately, narrower "plurilateral" arrangements can help, provided that they are explicitly designed to strengthen democracy.

proj-syn.title: The People Not Worth Replacing
proj-syn.description: At first glance, MAGA’s fear of immigrants and the rest of America’s fear of data centers have many similarities, with each reflecting insecurities about one’s place in a changing economy. But while the first fear tells natives that their place is valuable, the second assumes that it will soon be worth nothing.

proj-syn.title: What Amodei’s Call for an AI Pause Gets Wrong
proj-syn.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s recent appeal for a pause on AI development is a welcome one. But while AI companies do indeed need more breathing space to consider the full impact of their inventions before releasing them to the market, self-interested oversight is not the kind of governance we need.

proj-syn.title: Who Is Responsible for Nepal’s Tragedy?
proj-syn.description: The devastating floods in Nepal demonstrate what happens when reckless development puts climate-vulnerable communities in harm’s way. They also highlight a climate-finance system that is unable to provide the funds countries need in the immediate aftermath of such disasters.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Choose Between Power and Dependence
proj-syn.description: European citizens do not want “more Europe” in the abstract, but rather a European Union that is capable of protecting, investing, anticipating, deciding, and acting whenever national-level policymaking is insufficient. In today’s world, ensuring citizens’ control over their future requires the freedom to act together.

proj-syn.title: Progressive Economics Is Delivering
proj-syn.description: By combining fiscal responsibility, growth, and social development, progressive governments in Brazil and Spain have improved millions of people’s lives and refuted the hoary belief that conservatives are better stewards of the economy. Such a successful alternative model could not have come at a better time.

proj-syn.title: The Agentic Information Economy
proj-syn.description: An internet populated and run by AI agents will need not just reliable data but also a broader information ecology capable of questioning its own inputs and transmitting corrections where they are needed if information changes. But whether this will serve private interests or the public good remains to be seen.

proj-syn.title: Who Owns What AI Learns?
proj-syn.description: Since frontier AI models have already consumed much of the readily available stock of public knowledge on the internet, what remains is the valuable tacit knowledge embedded within organizations. Whoever sets the terms of how this knowledge is teased out and transferred will set the terms of the next economy.

proj-syn.title: America First Is Jeopardizing Taiwan’s Greatest Asset
proj-syn.description: Rather than strengthening Taiwan, US demands for market access, technology investment, and defense capabilities are deepening political polarization and eroding the island’s ability to build consensus just when it needs it most. The timing could hardly be worse.

proj-syn.title: Technology Is Not Above the Law
proj-syn.description: In arguing for a regulatory regime that is skewed entirely toward freeing developers to build online services, rather than placing any social obligations on them, the AI industry is using a playbook that Silicon Valley wrote 30 years ago. This time, however, the public seems less inclined to buy the industry's argument.

proj-syn.title: China’s Platform State and the AI Race
proj-syn.description: Balancing regulation with innovation is never easy, and the Chinese government’s robust support for AI could lead to inefficiency and excess. But the “platform state” model, combined with other strengths, has enabled China to achieve dominance in multiple strategic sectors, while enhancing its resilience.

proj-syn.title: Which Future for Online Life?
proj-syn.description: By articulating a vision of the future that seems inevitable, technology industry leaders want to create the impression that the surrender of privacy and other defining trends of the current moment cannot be stopped. But predictions become self-fulfilling prophecies only if we believe them and act accordingly.

proj-syn.title: When Words Are No Longer for Us
proj-syn.description: Owing to the proliferation of large language models throughout our software and social systems, we are now undergoing a textpocalypse, marked by not just a deluge of slop but a fundamental unmooring of language and text from lived human experience. The first victim is likely to be the internet itself.

proj-syn.title: Who Will Do the World’s “Most Impossible Job”?
proj-syn.description: Although the United Nations is facing a financial and political crisis that is almost certain to get worse before it gets better, the field of candidates vying for the organization’s top job is surprisingly crowded. If history is any guide, power politics, more than anything else, will decide the outcome.
